ca_wine_country.blurb: Wine Country spreads across Napa, Sonoma and the neighbouring coast ranges north of the Bay Area, with crags on rolling inland hills and others right at the ocean. Bouldering makes up about half the climbing, sport is roughly a third, and there is a smaller share of trad and top-rope. Boulder problems run from easy to the V5 range with a few harder; the sport climbing centres on 5.10 and 5.11, with a decent number of moderates and some 5.12. Mount St. Helena is the sport hub, with a steep bubble-shaped face, a bolted wall for the hard stuff and gentler top-rope terrain, all reached by long hikes. Salt Point and Sonoma Coast add seaside bouldering and sport, and the Nut Tree Boulders are a big bouldering zone.

co_rmnp_rock.blurb: Rocky Mountain National Park holds granite faces, pillars and high peaks around Estes Park, and the climbing here is far more alpine than most areas. Alpine routes and bouldering are the two largest groups, followed by ice and mixed lines, with a smaller amount of trad. Rock routes cluster around 5.9 to 5.11, with some 5.12 and a handful of harder ones, while the boulder problems run from V0 up through the V10s and beyond. Ice climbs mostly sit in the WI3 to WI5 range. Glacier Gorge, Longs Peak and Hallett Peak anchor the big-mountain climbing, and Wild Basin has a large bouldering collection. Summer and fall bring the most moderate weather, though snow can linger high up into July and afternoon storms arrive fast.

ca_indian_cove.blurb: Indian Cove sits in the northern part of Joshua Tree National Park, set apart from the rest of the park with its own turn-off from the highway. It is mostly a trad area, with a good number of sport routes, plenty of bouldering and a fair amount of top-rope. Most climbs fall between 5.6 and 5.11, peaking around 5.10, and there are plenty of easier lines for newer leaders along with a few 5.12s. The granite is somewhat grainier than in the main park and gets more crumbly toward the north. The cove is relatively sheltered and about a thousand feet lower than the main park, which makes it a good bet on cold winter days; winter, spring and fall are the favored seasons, and many formations face south. Rattlesnake Canyon is its biggest side area.

az_northern_az_bouldering.blurb: Northern Arizona bouldering is centred on Flagstaff, with dozens of boulder areas within a short drive of town, and Sedona as a smaller option nearby. The problems are almost all boulders, spread widely: plenty from V0 to V5 with a long tail into the V8 to V13 range. The stone varies by area, with basalt around town and at Turkey Tanks, dacite on Mt. Elden and the San Francisco Peaks, pocketed limestone roofs at places like Priest Draw, and sandstone at Kelly Canyon and the Anvil Boulders near Sedona. The mild, sunny climate allows bouldering all year, and sheltered roofs can stay dry even on winter days. Some areas are close to town, while others need a longer drive or walk.

or_willamette_valley.blurb: The Willamette Valley stretches roughly from Salem down to Cottage Grove, from the Coast Range east into the national forest. No single crag dominates; instead there are dozens of locally loved areas. Sport climbing is the largest share, closely followed by bouldering, with a smaller amount of trad and a little top-rope, ice and aid. Sport routes mostly sit in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, and boulder problems run from V0 to the V10s. The Garden is the main bouldering zone, while Eagles Rest and Lookout Point are major sport walls. Wolf Rock has big multi-pitch trad, Skinner Butte offers short basalt columns right in Eugene for top-rope or trad, and Marys Peak has mossy slabs and pillars.

ca_santa_barbara.blurb: The Santa Barbara area climbs in canyons and crags around the city, some of them inside the Los Padres National Forest. Bouldering accounts for over half the climbing, with sport and trad making up most of the rest and a little top-rope. Boulder problems range from easy to V10 with the bulk at moderate levels, and roped climbs mostly sit at 5.7 to 5.12, centred on 5.10. Gibraltar is a collection of single-pitch sandstone crags, while Potter's Point is a major bouldering area. The Playground offers short sport routes, and San Ysidro mixes slabs and steeper lines in a canyon where thick foliage can keep rock wet after heavy rain.
